Authentication and secure use

Source: vignettes/authentication.Rmd
authentication.Rmd

Why authentication is required

The TÜİK SDMX REST data service currently requires authentication. tuiksdmx accepts an API key and obtains a Bearer access token for requests internally. Anonymous calls to the service were observed to return HTTP 401 during package development. This describes observed service behaviour, not a permanent guarantee about the provider’s policy.

Do not publish API keys or access tokens. Never include real credentials in R Markdown files, Git repositories, examples, issue reports or logs. All examples here use placeholder values or assume the key was obtained through a secure mechanism. This vignette does not contact the live service when built.

Choosing how to supply an API key

Three approaches are supported. Using .Renviron is recommended, not required. If you supply api_key explicitly, the R variable holding it can have any name.

Option 1 — Persistent environment variable (recommended)

Open your personal R environment file:

usethis::edit_r_environ()

Add a line to your personal .Renviron file (this is a file entry, not an R command):

TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY=YOUR_OWN_KEY

Save the file and restart R. Do not add .Renviron to version control. When api_key is omitted (or NULL), tuiksdmx reads Sys.getenv("TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY") internally.

# No explicit api_key argument needed
cpi <- tuiksdmx::tuik_get_data(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01"
)

The exact environment variable name TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY is required only for this automatic lookup mechanism. It is not a required name for an ordinary R variable.

Option 2 — Supply the key explicitly

If you have obtained your key through a secure, untracked process and stored it in an R object called api, pass it to an authenticated function:

# Assume `api` already contains your valid key as one character string.
# Never paste a real key into source code that will be shared or committed.
profile <- tuiksdmx::tuik_flow_profile(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  api_key = api
)

cpi <- tuiksdmx::tuik_get_data(
  profile,
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01",
  api_key = api
)

The explicit api_key argument takes precedence over TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY. When using more than one authenticated function, provide the same key to each relevant call; passing a profile does not automatically mean all subsequent requests inherit the key that was used to create it.

Option 3 — Set the environment variable for this R session

When you already have a key in an R object called api:

Sys.setenv(TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY = api)

cpi <- tuiksdmx::tuik_get_data(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01"
)

Sys.setenv() changes the current R process environment and does not write to .Renviron. You will need to repeat it in a new session unless you have another persistent configuration mechanism. If you want to clear the variable from the current R process, use Sys.unsetenv("TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY") (but be aware that this also removes the environment value that may have been loaded from .Renviron for the remainder of the session).

What the package does with the key

The internal request layer resolves an explicitly provided key or reads TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY; it requests an access token and uses Bearer authentication for SDMX calls. Access tokens are cached separately by credential within the R session. When the authentication response provides a token expiry interval, the package records it; it also has a one-time token-refresh path for an HTTP 401 response. Users normally do not need to request, copy, print or manage access tokens themselves.

Because tokens and relevant metadata caches are in-memory session state, a new R process may need to authenticate and retrieve metadata again. Never assume authentication is permanent or that a successful request guarantees the next request will have the same latency.

Credentials in reproducible analyses

A script or report should describe which environment variable to set or which function argument to supply, but never include the actual credential:

# Example: reproducible query without a hard-coded secret.
# Requires the user to configure TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY beforehand.
result <- tuiksdmx::tuik_get_data(
  "DF_TUFE_SDMX_TT01",
  start_period = "2026-01",
  end_period = "2026-01"
)

For a report meant to be built offline, separate any live API retrieval from document rendering or use appropriately documented local fixture data. All network-dependent chunks in this vignette have eval = FALSE by default.

Troubleshooting

  • TUIK_SDMX_API_KEY was not found: provide api_key = ..., set the variable with Sys.setenv() in the current session, or configure .Renviron and restart R.
  • Invalid API key: supply one non-empty character string; ensure it has the required service access. Avoid printing it while diagnosing problems.
  • HTTP 401: the credential may be invalid, expired or rejected by the service. The package may retry once with a refreshed token; persistent failures need investigation of the credential and service permissions.
  • Intermittent long requests: timings may vary due to authentication, network, retries or service conditions. In development, some small requests finished in about one second and others took over 60 seconds; the exact cause was not established.

For dataset discovery and retrieval examples, see Getting started. For details on broader requests, see Filtering and performance.
